# Positive-part weighted fillings in the sharp radial density class

This records two exact closure calculations for the new continuous-filling
probe. It does NOT supply a sufficient mass lower bound for general OC.

## 1. Actual pointed geometry and continuous filling

Suppose an actual compatible family has an affine homothetic outer envelope

    C_z subset y(z)+ell(z)D,

where ell is positive affine on the compact full base projection and y is
affine. Set D_z=(C_z-y(z))/ell(z). For a pointed coordinate xi define

    A_xi={z:xi belongs to D_z}.

For fixed xi this is a convex base section, since z ->
(z,y(z)+ell(z)xi) is affine. The sampled pointed density is

    f(xi)=sum_(z in P) ell(z)^d 1_(D_z)(xi).

Use relative base coordinates of full rank n. For any c>=0 define

    G_c(xi)=integral_(A_xi) (ell(z)-c)_+^d dz.          (1)

If nonzero, G_c has a bounded compact convex positive support and its
extended inverse-(d+1)-st power is convex. This is an ORDINARY density
statement; no lattice change is made in the sampled comparison.

To verify it, translate the real base origin and scale ell so the
calculation has ell(z)=1+b.z. Apply the ordinary projective change

    t=z/ell(z),      xi=(x-y(z))/ell(z).

Its image of C is convex because its denominator is positive. Write
A(t)=1-b.t, so ell=1/A and dz=A^(-n-1)dt. Equation (1) is the xi
marginal of the joint density

    (1-c A)_+^d A^(-n-d-1)

on that convex projective image. Put beta=n+d+1 and theta=d/beta.
On its positive support the inverse beta-th root is

    h(A)=A/(1-c A)^theta.

For A>0 and c A<1,

    h''(A)=theta c (1-c A)^(-theta-2)
                         [2-(1-theta)c A] >=0.

For c=0 this is affine. The positive domain is the intersection of
convex halfspaces with the convex projective body. Thus the extended
inverse root is convex. Integrating the n base coordinates subtracts
n from beta in the proved inverse-power marginal theorem, leaving
the exact exponent d+1. General positive affine ell changes only
positive constant factors in this calculation.

## 2. Subtracting a constant preserves this density class

Let G be a nonnegative density whose extended inverse beta-th root h
is convex, beta>0. For C>=0 put g=(G-C)_+. On the positive domain of g,

    g^(-1/beta)=h/(1-C h^beta)^(1/beta).

For 0<h<C^(-1/beta), the right side is an increasing convex function
of h: its first derivative is (1-C h^beta)^(-1/beta-1), and its second
derivative is (beta+1)C h^(beta-1)(1-C h^beta)^(-1/beta-2).
The positive domain {h<C^(-1/beta)} is convex. Extension by infinity
outside that domain therefore proves inverse-power convexity of g.
The case C=0 is immediate. If g is nonzero, bounded and compactly
supported, the proved radial-centering theorem supplies its sharp
Gamma_r center in its r-dimensional full support.

## 3. One-dimensional base quadrature gives a genuine minorant

Let n=1, ell(z)=a+bz with b>0, and suppose every pointed occupancy
interval A_xi contains a fixed source interval with left integer
endpoint p_-. For c=b the weight in (1) is ell(z-1)_+^d.

Write k_0=ceil(inf A_xi), k_1=floor(sup A_xi). On each complete or
partial unit cell [k,k+1], k_0<=k<=k_1, the integrand is at most
ell(k)^d. Those cells contribute at most the sampled sum f(xi).
The only uncharged cell is the initial partial interval preceding
k_0. Its length is at most one, and its integrand is at most
ell(k_0-1)_+^d<=ell(p_-)^d because k_0<=p_-.
Consequently

    G_b(xi)<=f(xi)+ell(p_-)^d.

The nonnegative density

    g(xi)=(G_b(xi)-ell(p_-)^d)_+

is a genuine pointwise minorant of f and, by Sections 1--2, belongs
to the sharp inverse-(d+1)-power radial class whenever nonzero.
For b<0 reflect the base and use the smaller-scale source endpoint;
for b=0 the separate unweighted interval-count construction is sharper.

The missing step is quantitative: no proof here gives integral g>=M/2
in general. Naive estimates lose two terminal weights, and their
integrated cost cannot be replaced by a heavy-fiber bound without a
further argument. The closure and domination statements above are
proved; this mass comparison is explicitly not.
